mechanism_narrative: Persistently low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.1% compresses equity discount rates, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors shift from fixed income to equities.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS remains below 0.1% (measured via 12-month rolling windows).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 0.2 percentage points signals labor market tightening, boosting consumer spending and corporate earnings, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE declines by >0.2pp month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in real consumer spending (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 0.5% month-over-month indicates robust aggregate demand, accelerating corporate revenue growth and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and HOUST both rise > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: The joint signal (RSAFS and HOUST both rising >0.5%) fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production (INDPRO) falling below 98.0 indicates supply chain disruption, increasing input costs and reducing output, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO < 98.0, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 2-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: Year-over-year growth in real consumer spending (RSAFS) above 3.0% indicates sustained economic momentum, supporting equity valuations and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when RSAFS grows >3.0% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPIAUCSL increase exceeding 0.5 percentage points signals accelerating inflation, triggering anticipated monetary tightening and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL rises >0.5pp month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: Year-over-year growth in employment (PAYEMS) above 5.0% indicates labor market tightness, supporting consumer spending and corporate earnings, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS grows >5.0% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 0.5% month-over-month indicate broad supply shock, increasing input costs and reducing output, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO and HOUST both fall > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: The joint signal (INDPRO and HOUST both falling >0.5%) fails to produce negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or Rank IC > -0.03 over 3-year windows.
